title: Vue tracks reads; versions matter
outcome: Explain refs, computed values, watchers, and Vue 2 versus Vue 3 change detection.
version: Portable JavaScript · React hooks · Vue 2/3 comparisons · Next App Router

exercises.title: Find and fix the bug
exercises.prompt: A Vue 3 composable returns a reactive object. A caller destructures a numeric property and it stops updating. Repair the interface.

exercises.title: Change one condition
exercises.prompt: A Vue 2 form adds errors.title after the object is observed and the UI does not update. What is the version-aware repair?

trace.title: Reactive source
trace.detail: Vue tracks reactive reads and updates dependents when those values change. In Vue 3, reactive uses proxies for objects and ref holds a value accessed as .value in JavaScript. A computed value derives a result and caches it until tracked dependencies change.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
state.count is read through the proxy inside computed, so the dependency is tracked. Destructuring a primitive copies the current value into a plain variable. toRefs creates a linked access wrapper instead.

For a watcher, trace input change → old cleanup → new request → latest accepted result. onWatcherCleanup is a newer Vue 3 API; the callback cleanup parameter is another version-dependent choice. Do not paste it into Vue 2.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: A deep watcher is not free: it can traverse much data. Replacing computed with a watcher can add stale state. In Vue 2, setting list[index] directly has different detection behavior from splice.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Explain refs, computed values, watchers, and Vue 2 versus Vue 3 change detection. Give a concrete failure example.
